spec.expr:
# A container restart counted once, at one step, at any zoom level. Every
# container in the environment: Redis or Postgres are the likelier to be
# OOM-killed here. Restarts in a pod's first 5 minutes are skipped: they
# belong to its rollout (a dependency not ready yet), and a counter new
# within the window is counted in full by increase().
(
  increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{exported_namespace="$Environment"}[$__interval]) > 0
    unless on (exported_namespace, exported_pod)
    (time() - kube_pod_created{exported_namespace="$Environment"} < 300)
)
  # ...whose last termination was an OOM kill.
  and on (exported_namespace, exported_pod, container)
  kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason{reason="OOMKilled"} == 1

# A container restart counted once, at one step, at any zoom level. Every
# container in the environment: Redis or Postgres are the likelier to be
# OOM-killed here. Restarts in a pod's first 5 minutes are skipped: they
# belong to its rollout (a dependency not ready yet), and a counter new
# within the window is counted in full by increase().
(
  increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{exported_namespace="$Environment"}[$__interval]) > 0
    unless on (exported_namespace, exported_pod)
    (time() - kube_pod_created{exported_namespace="$Environment"} < 300)
)
  # ...for any other reason: probes, crashes, errors.
  unless on (exported_namespace, exported_pod, container)
  kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason{reason="OOMKilled"} == 1

# A new image_spec (the image as written in the pod spec) that wasn't
# running one step earlier: one point per rollout, at any zoom level.
# Not `image`: builds with no code change produce identical images, and
# the runtime then reports whichever tag it pulled first for them.
label_replace(
  count by (image_spec) (kube_pod_container_info{exported_namespace="$Environment", container="api"})
    unless count by (image_spec) (kube_pod_container_info{exported_namespace="$Environment", container="api"} offset $__interval),
  "version", "$1", "image_spec", ".*:(.+)"
)

# k6 streams its metrics while a run is going (test:load:*:dev), tagged
# with the namespace it targets and a test id: one region per run.
max by (testid) (k6_vus{namespace="$Environment"})

sum by(pod) (rate(container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total{namespace="$Environment", pod=~"url-shortener-api-.*", container="api"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by(pod) (rate(container_cpu_cfs_periods_total{namespace="$Environment", pod=~"url-shortener-api-.*", container="api"}[$__rate_interval]))) * 100

spec.title: p99 latency: request vs. dependencies
spec.description: Where a request spends its time. If HTTP rises and a dependency rises with it, that dependency is the bottleneck. If HTTP rises alone, look at the API itself (CPU, throttling). Dashed red: the timeouts from the config. Log scale.

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_project="url-shortener", grncunha_com_service="api", route!~"/metrics|GET /healthz"}[$__rate_interval])))

spec.title: CPU usage, % of limit
spec.description: Averaged over the rate window, so bursts shorter than that are smoothed away: a container can be well under its limit here and still be paused many times a second. Check CPU throttling next to it.

spec.expr: 100 * sum by (pod, container) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{namespace="$Environment", container=~"api|postgres|redis"}[$__rate_interval])) / on (pod, container) sum by (pod, container) (label_replace(kube_pod_container_resource_limits{exported_namespace="$Environment", container=~"api|postgres|redis", resource="cpu"}, "pod", "$1", "exported_pod", "(.*)"))

spec.title: CPU throttling
spec.description: Share of 100ms CFS periods in which the container used up its CPU quota and was paused until the next period. Counted by the kernel, so no pause is missed between scrapes. Any sustained value means requests are stalling, even when average CPU looks low.

spec.expr: 100 * sum by (pod, container) (rate(container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total{namespace="$Environment", container=~"api|postgres|redis"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (pod, container) (rate(container_cpu_cfs_periods_total{namespace="$Environment", container=~"api|postgres|redis"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.title: Memory, % of limit
spec.description: The container is OOM-killed at 100%.

spec.expr: 100 * sum by (pod, container) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace="$Environment", container=~"api|postgres|redis"}) / on (pod, container) sum by (pod, container) (label_replace(kube_pod_container_resource_limits{exported_namespace="$Environment", container=~"api|postgres|redis", resource="memory"}, "pod", "$1", "exported_pod", "(.*)"))

spec.title: Postgres pool: acquires that had to wait
spec.description: Share of connection requests that found no idle connection (waited), and that gave up (acquire timeout, a 503). Counted on every acquire, so pool exhaustion shows up even when it lasts milliseconds.

spec.title: Query latency (seen by the API)
spec.description: Time from sending the query to getting the result. Does not include waiting for a pool connection.

spec.title: API pool connections
spec.description: Snapshot: sampled once per scrape (15s), so it only shows the state at those instants and misses anything shorter. For waiting, see "API pool waits" and "API pool acquire time".

spec.title: API pool waits
spec.description: Acquires that found no free connection. Any sustained value here means the pool is too small, or queries hold connections too long.

spec.title: Server connections by state
spec.description: "active" is connections running a query right now. If it stays close to the pool size, Postgres itself is the bottleneck. If the pool is full but few are active, the time is spent in the API between queries. Snapshot: sampled once per scrape (15s), so it only shows the state at those instants and misses anything shorter.

spec.title: Buffer cache hit ratio
spec.description: Share of block reads served from shared_buffers. Below ~99% under load means queries go to disk.

spec.expr: 100 * sum(rate(cnpg_pg_stat_database_blks_hit{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_service="db", datname="app"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum(rate(cnpg_pg_stat_database_blks_hit{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_service="db", datname="app"}[$__rate_interval])) + sum(rate(cnpg_pg_stat_database_blks_read{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_service="db", datname="app"}[$__rate_interval])))

spec.title: Latency: API vs. Redis server
spec.description: Server time is only Redis executing the command. The gap to the API line is network, waiting for a pool connection, and the API being slow to schedule (CPU throttling).

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, cmd) (rate(redis_commands_latencies_usec_bucket{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_service="cache", cmd=~"get|set"}[$__rate_interval]))) / 1e6

spec.title: API pool connections
spec.description: go-redis pool size defaults to 10 × GOMAXPROCS. Snapshot: sampled once per scrape (15s), so it only shows the state at those instants and misses anything shorter.

spec.expr: sum by (pod) (redis_pool_conn_total_current{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_project="url-shortener", grncunha_com_service="api"} - redis_pool_conn_idle_current{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_project="url-shortener", grncunha_com_service="api"})

spec.title: API pool pressure
spec.description: Misses mean a new connection had to be opened. Timeouts mean the pool was full and a command waited too long.

spec.title: Redis CPU
spec.description: Redis runs commands on one thread, so it can never use more than 1 core for them.

spec.title: Cache hit ratio
spec.description: Every miss becomes a Postgres query. A falling hit ratio moves load onto Postgres.

spec.title: Clients
spec.description: Snapshot: sampled once per scrape (15s), so it only shows the state at those instants and misses anything shorter.

spec.title: Dependency timeouts
spec.description: Log lines that carry a `dependency` field: 503s (ERROR "dependency timeout") and cache failures that fell back to Postgres (WARN "cache read/write failed").

spec.expr: {kubernetes.pod_namespace="$Environment", kubernetes.container_name="api"} dependency:* | stats by (dependency, operation) count() timeouts

spec.title: Postgres logs
spec.description: Includes checkpoints, which can line up with latency spikes. CNPG wraps each Postgres line in a JSON "record"; it is rewritten here as "<severity>: <message>".

spec.title: API pool acquire time
spec.description: Time a query waited for a connection from the pool, from a histogram of every acquire. Near zero while idle connections are available; grows as soon as the pool runs dry.

spec.title: Requests waiting for a connection (avg)
spec.description: Total time spent waiting for a pool connection per second, which equals the average number of requests queued for one (Little's law). From a counter, so short queues between scrapes still count.

spec.title: Requests per second: k6 sent vs. API handled
spec.description: A gap between the two lines is requests lost or still in flight between k6 and the API: network, gateway, or connections that never opened. k6 lines are increase()/window, not rate(): k6's series start and stop mid-test (one per phase), which rate() counts twice while they overlap.

spec.title: Failures: k6 vs. API
spec.description: k6 counts a request as failed on an unexpected status or a transport error (dial timeouts, resets), which the API never sees. Dropped iterations: k6 had no free VU to start one on time, so the target rate was not reached. k6 lines are increase()/window, not rate(): k6's series start and stop mid-test (one per phase), which rate() counts twice while they overlap.

spec.title: k6 virtual users
spec.description: VUs in use vs. allocated. An arrival-rate test adds VUs when responses slow down, so a climbing line means requests are taking longer.

spec.title: Data sent and received by k6
spec.description: k6 lines are increase()/window, not rate(): k6's series start and stop mid-test (one per phase), which rate() counts twice while they overlap.

spec.title: k6 p99 per test (successful requests, steady phase)
spec.description: Latency of successful requests as k6 measured it, from the laptop: network and gateway included. Cumulative over the steady phase, so it matches k6's end-of-test http_req_duration{ expected_response:true }. Failed requests (timeouts, 5xx) are in "Failures: k6 vs. API".

spec.expr: max by (testid, method) (last_over_time(k6_http_req_duration_p99{namespace="$Environment", testid=~"$LoadTest", phase="steady", expected_response="true"}[$__range]))

spec.title: API p99 over the selected time range
spec.description: Latency inside the API, over the whole selected range. Zoom the time range to a single test for a like-for-like comparison with k6's p99: the difference is the network and gateway.

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, route) (increase(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_project="url-shortener", grncunha_com_service="api", route!~"/metrics|GET /healthz"}[$__range])))

spec.title: Where k6's request time goes (p99, cumulative)
spec.description: Blocked: waiting for a free connection in k6. Connecting / TLS: opening one. Sending and receiving: the bytes. Waiting: from the request sent to the first byte back, i.e. network round trip plus everything on the server. Successful requests only, per method.

spec.title: k6 latency since the test started
spec.description: Cumulative since the start of each test: the line settles on the test's final value rather than following the current latency. Use the API panels for latency over time. Successful requests only.

spec.expr: max by (testid, method) (k6_http_req_duration_p50{namespace="$Environment", testid=~"$LoadTest", phase="steady", expected_response="true"})
max by (testid, method) (k6_http_req_duration_p99{namespace="$Environment", testid=~"$LoadTest", phase="steady", expected_response="true"})

spec.title: Peak requests per second
spec.description: Over the selected time range.

spec.title: Errors (5xx)
spec.description: Over the selected time range. Share of requests answered with 5xx.

spec.expr: 100 * sum(increase(http_requests_total{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_project="url-shortener", grncunha_com_service="api", status=~"5.."}[$__range])) / sum(increase(http_requests_total{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_project="url-shortener", grncunha_com_service="api", route!~"/metrics|GET /healthz"}[$__range]))

spec.title: p99 latency
spec.description: Over the selected time range. Inside the API. Yellow at 100ms, red at 500ms: the load tests' targets.

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (increase(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_project="url-shortener", grncunha_com_service="api", route!~"/metrics|GET /healthz"}[$__range])))

spec.title: Peak API CPU, % of limit
spec.description: Over the selected time range. Averaged over the rate window: short bursts are smoothed away. See the scheduler tile.

spec.title: Peak API CPU pressure
spec.description: Over the selected time range. Share of time the container had work ready but was waiting for CPU (kernel CPU pressure): hitting its CPU limit, or a busy node. From a counter, so short waits count.

spec.title: Peak requests waiting for a connection
spec.description: Over the selected time range. Average number of requests queued for a Postgres or Redis pool connection. Anything sustained above zero means a pool, or the API holding its connections, is the limit.

spec.title: CPU pressure: % of time waiting for CPU
spec.description: Share of time the container had work ready but was waiting for CPU (kernel CPU pressure): hitting its CPU limit, or a busy node. From a counter, so short waits count.

spec.title: Requests waiting for a connection (avg)
spec.description: Time spent waiting for a pool connection, per second: the average number of requests queued (Little's law). From counters, so short queues count. Redis only counts waits that got a connection: waits that timed out show up in "Failures by cause".

spec.title: Average time per request, by part
spec.description: Stacked, the parts add up to the average request time (dashed). "API itself" is the rest: its own CPU work and waiting for a thread. Redis waits cut short by a timeout count as "Redis command". Averages, not p99: percentiles can't be stacked.

spec.expr: clamp_min(sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_project="url-shortener", grncunha_com_service="api", route!~"/metrics|GET /healthz"}[$__rate_interval])) - sum(rate(pg_pool_acquire_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_project="url-shortener", grncunha_com_service="api"}[$__rate_interval])) - sum(rate(pg_query_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_project="url-shortener", grncunha_com_service="api"}[$__rate_interval])) - sum(rate(redis_query_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_project="url-shortener", grncunha_com_service="api"}[$__rate_interval])), 0) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_project="url-shortener", grncunha_com_service="api", route!~"/metrics|GET /healthz"}[$__rate_interval]))

sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_project="url-shortener", grncunha_com_service="api", route!~"/metrics|GET /healthz"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_project="url-shortener", grncunha_com_service="api", route!~"/metrics|GET /healthz"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.title: Failures by cause
spec.description: Postgres failures become 503s (dashed). Redis failures don't: the API falls back to Postgres (see "Reads"), which adds load there instead.

spec.expr: sum(rate(pg_query_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_project="url-shortener", grncunha_com_service="api", outcome=~"error"}[$__rate_interval])) + sum(rate(pg_pool_acquire_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_project="url-shortener", grncunha_com_service="api", outcome=~"error"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.title: Reads: Redis vs. Postgres fallback
spec.description: How each short-URL lookup was answered. A miss is normal (the key isn't cached); a Redis failure also falls back to Postgres, adding load there.

spec.title: API pool waits
spec.description: Commands that had to wait for a free connection, and the average number waiting. Only waits that got a connection: those cut short by a timeout are Redis timeouts in "Commands per second by outcome".

spec.title: CPU pressure: % of time waiting for CPU
spec.description: Share of time the container had work ready but was waiting for CPU (kernel CPU pressure): hitting its CPU limit, or a busy node. From a counter, so short waits count.

spec.title: Postgres pool health
spec.description: In use: average share of the pool's connections held (not a snapshot). Wait share: of the time requests spend on the pool, the share spent queueing for a connection. Idle while held: share of the time a connection is held without a query running on it, e.g. while the request waits for CPU. High wait share with low idle: the pool is too small. High idle: the API holds connections it isn't using. A pool that freezes briefly shows a high wait share with only moderate in use: every queued request adds to the waiting, while holding is capped at the pool size.

spec.title: Redis pool health
spec.description: In use: average share of the pool's connections held (not a snapshot). Wait share: of the time requests spend on the pool, the share spent queueing for a connection. Held but not in Redis: share of the time a connection is held while Redis isn't working on the command (network, and the API itself). Approximate: Redis' own time comes from the exporter. Wait share only counts waits that got a connection: timed-out waits show up as Redis timeouts. A pool that freezes briefly shows a high wait share with only moderate in use: every queued request adds to the waiting, while holding is capped at the pool size.

spec.expr: 100 * clamp_min(clamp_min(sum(rate(redis_query_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_project="url-shortener", grncunha_com_service="api"}[$__rate_interval])) - sum(rate(redis_pool_wait_seconds_total{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_project="url-shortener", grncunha_com_service="api"}[$__rate_interval])), 0) - sum(rate(redis_commands_duration_seconds_total{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_service="cache", cmd=~"get|set"}[$__rate_interval])), 0) / clamp_min(sum(rate(redis_query_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_project="url-shortener", grncunha_com_service="api"}[$__rate_interval])) - sum(rate(redis_pool_wait_seconds_total{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_project="url-shortener", grncunha_com_service="api"}[$__rate_interval])), 0)

spec.title: Postgres pool health
spec.description: In use: average share of the pool's connections held (not a snapshot). Wait share: of the time requests spend on the pool, the share spent queueing for a connection. Idle while held: share of the time a connection is held without a query running on it, e.g. while the request waits for CPU. High wait share with low idle: the pool is too small. High idle: the API holds connections it isn't using. A pool that freezes briefly shows a high wait share with only moderate in use: every queued request adds to the waiting, while holding is capped at the pool size.

spec.title: Redis pool health
spec.description: In use: average share of the pool's connections held (not a snapshot). Wait share: of the time requests spend on the pool, the share spent queueing for a connection. Held but not in Redis: share of the time a connection is held while Redis isn't working on the command (network, and the API itself). Approximate: Redis' own time comes from the exporter. Wait share only counts waits that got a connection: timed-out waits show up as Redis timeouts. A pool that freezes briefly shows a high wait share with only moderate in use: every queued request adds to the waiting, while holding is capped at the pool size.

spec.expr: 100 * clamp_min(clamp_min(sum(rate(redis_query_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_project="url-shortener", grncunha_com_service="api"}[$__rate_interval])) - sum(rate(redis_pool_wait_seconds_total{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_project="url-shortener", grncunha_com_service="api"}[$__rate_interval])), 0) - sum(rate(redis_commands_duration_seconds_total{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_service="cache", cmd=~"get|set"}[$__rate_interval])), 0) / clamp_min(sum(rate(redis_query_duration_seconds_sum{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_project="url-shortener", grncunha_com_service="api"}[$__rate_interval])) - sum(rate(redis_pool_wait_seconds_total{namespace="$Environment", grncunha_com_project="url-shortener", grncunha_com_service="api"}[$__rate_interval])), 0)

spec.title: New connections per second, gateway → API
spec.description: The gateway talks to the API over HTTP/1.1: one connection per request in flight. A spike means a burst of concurrent requests (e.g. k6 starting many VUs at once), each paying for a new connection through the mesh, and arriving at the API together.
